tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to gather information about the AI system they can use to plan future operations.

tactics.name: Resource Development
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.

tactics.name: AI Attack Adaptation
tactics.summary: The adversary is adapting capabilities, methods, knowledge, or objectives into attack-ready outputs for a target or current operational conditions.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to gain access to the AI system.

tactics.name: AI Model Access
tactics.summary: The adversary is attempting to gain some level of access to an AI model.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to run malicious code embedded in AI artifacts or software.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold via AI artifacts or software.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected by AI-enabled security software.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to figure out your AI environment.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to move through your AI environment.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to gather AI artifacts and other related information relevant to their goal.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised AI systems to control them.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to steal AI artifacts or other information about the AI system.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.summary: The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt, erode confidence in, or destroy your AI systems and data.

techniques.name: Search Open Websites/Domains
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search public websites and/or domains for information about victims and AI targets that can be used during targeting and to discover opportunities for successful attacks.

techniques.name: Code Repositories
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search public code repositories for information about a victim or victim system that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: AI Service API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using the API of an AI service on the victim's system.

mitigations.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data in Production

techniques.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to use their access to an AI agent on the victim's system to retrieve data from available agent tools to collect credentials.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Data Poisoning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate data in a victim-controlled, trusted, or connected data source that is accessible through an AI agent tool.

techniques.name: AI Agent Clickbait
techniques.summary: Adversaries may craft deceptive content designed to bait computer-using AI agents or AI web browsers and tools into taking unintended actions, such as clicking buttons, copying code, or navigating to specific web pages.

techniques.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may invoke an AI agent's tool capable of performing mutative operations to perform Data Destruction.

mitigations.name: Human In-the-Loop for AI Agent Actions
Restrict AI Agent Tool Invocation on Untrusted Data

techniques.name: Generate Malicious Commands
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use large language models (LLMs) to dynamically generate malicious commands from natural language.

techniques.name: Deploy AI Agent
techniques.summary: Adversaries may launch AI agents in the victim's environment to execute actions on their behalf.

techniques.name: Escape to Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may break out of a container or virtualized environment to gain access to the underlying host.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to collect credentials.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a system or application vulnerability to bypass security features.

techniques.name: AI Agent
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse AI agents present on the victim's system for command and control.

techniques.name: AI Supply Chain Rug Pull
techniques.summary: Adversaries may publish legitimate AI components or software, gain user adoption, then push an update with a malicious variant, leading to AI Supply Chain Compromise.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison tools used by AI agents by introducing or modifying malicious content or behavior in a tool's model-visible definition, executable implementation, or runtime responses.

techniques.name: Definition and Instructions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison the model-visible definition or operational instructions of an AI agent tool to manipulate how an agent interprets, selects, or invokes the tool.

techniques.name: Implementation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison the executable implementation of an AI agent tool so that normal tool invocation produces unauthorized behavior or hidden side effects.

techniques.name: Runtime Response
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison the runtime response channel of a malicious or compromised AI agent tool by deliberately returning content intended to influence the model's subsequent reasoning, decisions, or actions.

techniques.name: AI Supply Chain Reputation Inflation
techniques.summary: AI Supply Chain Reputation Inflation is the process of building or leveraging genuinely credible-looking trust signals to increase the perceived legitimacy of AI supply chain components, with the goal of driving adoptio…

techniques.name: Machine Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise a machine by exploiting or manipulating AI-enabled components on the system.

techniques.name: Local AI Agent
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve full system compromise by abusing AI agents running locally on a host, such as computer-use agents or AI-driven browsers.

techniques.name: AI Artifacts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve full system compromise by introducing malicious AI artifacts, such as models or data, that contain embedded malware or other malicious commands.

mitigations.name: Control Access to AI Models and Data at Rest

techniques.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal web application or service session cookies used to authenticate users to AI-enabled systems, AI services, or supporting enterprise applications.

techniques.name: AI Service Web Interface
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate with compromised systems by abusing the web interface of an AI service as an intermediary command-and-control relay.

techniques.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify AI artifacts and publish them through public or shared distribution channels to facilitate compromise of downstream AI systems.

techniques.name: Datasets
techniques.summary: Adversaries may publish poisoned datasets intended for training or fine-tuning AI models.

techniques.name: Models
techniques.summary: Adversaries may publish poisoned AI models through model registries, code repositories, or other model distribution channels.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create and publish poisoned AI agent tools.

techniques.name: Autonomous Reconnaissance
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use autonomous AI agents to conduct Reconnaissance activities.

techniques.name: Autonomous Attack-Path Adaptation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an AI agent to autonomously construct and repeatedly revise an attack path toward an adversary-defined objective.

techniques.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication
techniques.summary: Autonomous AI agents may exchange operational information with other AI agents, sub-agents, or independent agent runs.

techniques.name: Communication via Shared Artifacts
techniques.summary: Autonomous AI agents may communicate by creating or modifying artifacts in a shared resource that persists outside their individual execution contexts.

techniques.name: Direct Agent Communication
techniques.summary: Autonomous AI agents may communicate directly through agent-to-agent, sub-agent, or orchestrator interfaces.

techniques.name: Exploit Automated Artifact Processing Pipeline
techniques.summary: Adversaries may submit, publish, or modify an artifact in a way that triggers an automated processing pipeline.

techniques.name: AI Artifact Repository
techniques.summary: Adversaries may repurpose AI artifact repositories as asynchronous command-and-control channels.

techniques.name: AI Agent Environment Reconstruction
techniques.summary: An autonomous AI agent may reconstruct the environment needed to continue an existing operation after its execution environment is lost, reset, replaced, denied, or made unusable.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software or design weakness in a service reachable from their current environment to gain unauthorized access to another system, component, network, or trust boundary.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit.

techniques.name: Autonomous Attack Orchestration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use autonomous AI systems as an operational control layer to manage multiple distinct autonomous agents or sub-agents toward a common adversary-defined objective.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to an AI system or its supporting infrastructure.

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use automated techniques to collect data from AI systems and supporting enterprise environments.

techniques.name: Data Staged
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stage collected data in a central location before exfiltration.

techniques.name: Compromise Infrastructure
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise third-party infrastructure and repurpose it to support attacks against AI system.

techniques.name: Triggers in Multimodal Inputs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may place instructions or triggers in one part of a multimodal input to influence the model while staying unnoticed by human reviewers and by defenses that do not inspect all input modalities.

techniques.name: AI Agent Response Biasing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate an AI assistant so that it favors adversary-chosen sources, or content in its responses.

techniques.name: Crafted AI Assistant Links
techniques.summary: Adversaries may craft links that open an AI assistant or agent with attacker-controlled input already supplied, so that opening the link initiates an interaction the adversary defines rather than one the target composed.

techniques.name: Misconfigured or Publicly Exposed AI Services
techniques.summary: AI agents and LLM platforms are deployed across diverse architectures, including standalone servers, SaaS platforms, and low-code builders.

techniques.name: Discover AI Agent Runtime Capabilities
techniques.summary: Adversaries may interact with an AI agent at runtime to reveal the capabilities available to it, without requiring access to its underlying configuration.

techniques.name: AI Targeted Cloaking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may selectively deliver malicious or manipulated content to AI systems, while presenting different benign content to human users, web crawlers, or security detection mechanisms.
